items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

The world's largest crypto exchange said the attackers compromised a computer and an internal artificial intelligence tool to take control of its wallets.

It believes the theft, carried out on October 29, could be the largest-ever financial heist. The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the attack , a claim North Korea has rejected. Binance has said it is repaying all customers who have lost funds through the hack.

The company set out what went wrong in an initial report published on Tuesday. It described a sophisticated hacking endeavor that began with an advert for a tampered version of a coding tool in June. That download set in motion a series of security breaches which culminated in the theft of the crypto on October 29.

Binance logo is displayed on a phone screen adjacent to an image from a crypto exchange on a laptop ( Getty Images )

According to the report, the attack started when an employee from Binance's wallet developer team downloaded an AI tool in June that had been tampered with. The crypto exchange detected the compromise, replaced the device, and changed credentials. But the employee's role, and that of others on the wallet team, was exposed to the hacker. A second software engineer was targeted in September.

The engineer was seeking a new job and downloaded a "malicious code repository" onto his computer after interviewing for what he thought was a legitimate role. The interview process included a virtual meeting with the CEO of a fictitious company.

items.title: Safari introduces Adaptive Dark Mode in 27.3
items.content:
by Simon Fraser, Luming Yin, Lily Spiniolas, Joanne Pan, Veda Periwal and Jen Simmons

We’re excited to announce Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari 27.3 beta. When enabled by a user, Safari adapts light websites and presents them as dark.

In the spring of 2019, Safari 12.1 became the first browser to support dark mode on the web. A lot of people love using dark mode, but not every website has a dark version. Almost 40% of web page loads are from users in dark mode, and yet only 10% of page loads support it. If you love dark mode, you’ve probably hit a site that felt particularly bright . Adaptive Dark Mode is designed to close that gap, providing a consistent dark experience across the web.

You can try it today in Safari 27.3 beta. To enable, first make sure your system appearance is set to dark. Then browse to a website with a bright background. Safari will offer a preview of Adaptive Dark Mode. Tap ‘Try’.

For websites that signal support of dark mode with <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> in HTML or color-scheme: light dark in CSS, Adaptive Dark Mode does not change a thing. For the rest of the web, it quickly analyzes the page, looking at colors and estimating whether it’s predominantly light or dark. If the page generally has a dark background with light text, nothing is changed. When a page has a light appearance, Adaptive Dark Mode adapts the page to be dark.

At the core of Adaptive Dark Mode is the transformation of color. Sometimes colors are simply decorative, while other times they have semantic meaning. Adaptive Dark Mode determines when to invert colors so elements remain visible or when to leave colors unchanged.

While creating Adaptive Dark Mode, we developed a color matrix to invert the luminosity of colors while preserving hue. It’s used to make light backgrounds dark, and dark text light. When transforming text color, Adaptive Dark Mode aims for sufficient contrast as defined by the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio . Light CSS gradients are also transformed to dark.

Adaptive Dark Mode makes careful judgments so transformed content looks good and stays usable: buttons have contrast against backgrounds, text is visible over images, and hover menus look clear.

It takes the same care with images. Most are left unchanged, preserving their integrity. But many icons and logos can lose contrast when the background color behind them is inverted. So Adaptive Dark Mode inspects SVG images and transforms colors when needed. For bitmap images, it analyzes the pixel histograms and inverts simple black-and-white logos.

Effects like masks and mix-blend-mode can create undesirable results on an element whose colors have been transformed, so in some cases Adaptive Dark Mode turns such effects off. Also, <canvas> content is left unchanged, since canvases contain a wide range of content that’s hard to predict.

It’s precisely because Adaptive Dark Mode is happening deep within the WebKit browser engine that we are able to find creative ways to solve the most complex challenges, apply the transformations with great speed and power efficiency, all while rigorously protecting user privacy.

In general, a web page will work well with Adaptive Dark Mode if it follows good modern web development practices.

If your site still uses older techniques, small updates can help. For logos and icons, swap bitmap images for SVG. Use solid or gradient colors in CSS instead of tiled background images. Replace image sprites with modern CSS for rounded corners, shadows, and button states. Create content images with transparent backgrounds instead of baking the page background color into the image. Add padding to containers to prevent crowding.

Perhaps you want a specific dark mode experience for a certain portion of the page. Apply color-scheme: light dark to the relevant element and add your own dark styles.

For complete control over how your site looks in dark mode, add full support. It’s a terrific time to do so. It’s never been…

items.title: EU copyright overhaul risks forcing VPNs to police the internet — here's what we know
items.content:
(Image credit: Vlad Yushinov/via Getty Images)

The European Commission is considering EU-wide anti-piracy blocking orders as part of a Copyright Package due in 2027.

A tech industry group warns this could force VPN providers to inspect and filter their users' traffic.

France and Spain already make VPNs block pirate sites, and the results so far have been messy.

Europe's next big copyright shake-up could change how your VPN works behind the scenes, even if you never go near a pirate stream.

The European Commission is weighing an EU-wide system of anti-piracy injunctions that would require providers to block access to websites and servers hosting infringing content.

According to the Disruptive Competition Project (DisCo), a blog run by tech industry body CCIA, that system could sweep in VPN providers, including the services on our best VPN list.

The group argues this would turn privacy tools into internet watchdogs. The plans remain on the table for the Commission's Copyright Package, which is expected in the second quarter of 2027.

VPNs are built to be neutral. They route and encrypt your traffic without monitoring or controlling what you access, and they don't host any content themselves.

DisCo points out that blocking orders wouldn't break a VPN's encryption. However, enforcing them would require providers to check traffic against blocklists, such as destination IP addresses or DNS requests.

That shifts VPNs from passive conduits to active filters. And since the infringing content stays online, pirates can simply move to new domains or routes.

Several countries are already ahead of Brussels. In 2025, a Paris court ordered five major VPNs to block more than 200 illegal sports streaming sites, while Italy moved to extend its Piracy Shield system to VPN and DNS providers.

In Spain, a Córdoba court ordered NordVPN and Proton VPN to block IP addresses tied to illegal LaLiga streams in February.

The same court later refused to fine NordVPN for not complying. LaLiga has since asked the Commission to add NordVPN, Proton VPN, ExpressVPN, and Surfshark to its piracy watch list.

DisCo highlights the irony: Spain's national cybersecurity institute, INCIBE, actively recommends VPNs to citizens as a way to protect their personal data.

In July, the EU's top court ruled that VPNs are lawful technical tools and that providers aren't liable when users bypass geoblocking. That ruling dealt with liability, though, not blocking orders, so it doesn't stop an EU-wide injunction system from pulling VPNs in.

If that happens, the most obvious change is that some sites could become unreachable through your VPN. Overblocking is the bigger worry. IP blocking is a blunt tool, and LaLiga's campaign in Spain has already knocked hundreds of thousands of legitimate domains offline.

There's a privacy cost, too. Even light-touch rules to monitor, filter, or retain traffic would weaken the protections that private VPNs are built to offer.

For now, nothing is final. The Commission hasn't published its proposal, so the real test will come when the Copyright Package lands next year.

items.title: You’ll need nerves of steel to work with AI agents
items.content:
You’ll need nerves of steel to work with AI agents

This post will focus mainly on Composer 2.5 in Cursor. These problems may not be present in opus-5.5 or gpt-6.1-sol-pro-max-ultra-thinking-fast. But gpt-6.1-luna, for example, has all the problems listed here. I’ve also encountered many of these problems before in gpt-5.5 and opus-4.6. I don’t know whether they’re present in the newer AI models released recently.

What I like about Composer 2.5: its usage limits and speed.

For comparison, let’s take two $20 subscriptions, one for GPT and one for Cursor. With gpt-6.1-sol, my 5-hour limit runs out after just a few requests. If I ask it to change a couple of lines in a readme file, that uses up 10% of the limit. If I ask it to change something in a large codebase, the entire limit gets used up just reading dozens of files, without writing a single line of code.

But GPT also offers a $100 plan with five times the usage limits. And how long would that last me? I work with complex monorepo projects. To make changes to one service, the agent has to read dozens of files in other services and several skills. If the $20 plan runs out after reading 20 files, will the $100 plan run out after reading 100 files?

That’s why I don’t use Sol, but use Luna instead. But it’s very slow. Compared to Composer 2.5, it’s dozens of times slower.

That’s why I don’t use GPT Luna, but use Composer 2.5 instead. It’s very fast and very cheap. And in exchange for that speed and savings, I end up wasting my time and getting stressed out. I’ve encountered some of these problems in Deepseek and other open models. Some models have certain problems but not others. The number and frequency of problems vary even when using the same model, depending on the phase of the moon.

Below is a list of problems I’ve encountered over 100+ hours of working with Composer in Cursor.

The agent writes code and changes dozens of files. I start reviewing the code, and the following conversation ensues:

— You’re right. This function isn’t needed here. (Deletes the function and makes changes to many files)

— You’re right. I shouldn’t have deleted that function. I’m putting it back. (Makes changes to many files again)

And I still never got an answer to the question of why that function was needed.

Now, whenever I want to ask it something, I have to turn off agent mode or explicitly tell it not to delete anything. But when I forget to do that, it starts deleting parts of the code in response to a simple question.

Sometimes I spend a lot of time reviewing the code and ask it to change just one function. It changes all the files that have already been reviewed. And these changes don’t even relate to that function.

It might even delete all the work done in this chat. And not just in this one. I ask it to make a commit, and it finds changes to other files mixed in. And it just deletes them. Even though that work was done in other chats.

Also, if I ask it to refactor the code — for example, to rename a method in 50 files — it might delete all the comments it finds in those files. Which has absolutely nothing to do with refactoring the method.

And yet, it doesn’t delete what I ask it to delete. When changing a method’s name, it leaves the old method in place and adds a new one with the new name. That’s its entire refactoring process — so it doesn’t have to change all the files where the old method was called. It’ll simply mark the old method as deprecated and leave it accessible. If I point this out, it will finally do the refactoring, but leave the old method name in the tests and documentation. The tests will fail, and it will say the task is complete and the method has been refactored, but the tests are failing. As far as the agent is concerned, failing tests don’t count as evidence that the task is incomplete.

Also, while working on a task, it might remove an important parameter from the config or from a method that has nothing to do with the task at all. When asked why…

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: A Decade of Kill Bugs
items.summary: historical, linux, unix
items.content:
On the morning of September 24th 2026, Endcrawl had a brief outage. I'd just typed:

Right away I blamed myself. Maybe I mistyped that number! Maybe my code had a signal handling bug. Maybe I don't understand Unix as well as I think I do. Maybe I'm an idiot!

As it turned out, the outage was caused by a bug in kill(1) .

This is really surprising. The kill program is 50 years old. Its spec is simple and stable. It's probably exercised a billion times a day.

A bug in kill was so surprising that, once I'd found it, I couldn't stop there. I needed to know how this bug came to be, and what had led the programmers so badly astray. When I eventually found the root cause, there was an even bigger surprise. It had led to not just one bug, but a whole series of kill bugs that shipped in Ubuntu 14, 16, 18, 22 and 24 LTS.

This post documents a decade of kill bugs, then makes some recommendations.

Back to the outage. I scrambled to put the fire out. After that came a surprise second fire. By the end of all this I was pretty demoralized. I was ready to accept that I'd made a dumb mistake and ready to get on with the work day. There was this nagging feeling though…

Remember that final scene in Burn After Reading?

"I don't f**king know either. I guess we learned not to do it again."

"Although I'm f**ked if I know what we did..."

What had just happened? Was I about to be hit with a third outage? How could I be sure?

An outage not understood is an outage that happens again. That nagging feeling I had was a call to understand. With a sigh, I put all my other work on hold and started a proper post mortem.

Let's examine the command that caused the outage:

The negative number here is a process group identifier , or pgid for short. A pgid is like a pid, but identifies a group of related processes. By convention, killing a positive number sends a signal to a single process, while killing a negative number signals all processes in that process group.

I was attempting to cancel a big Endcrawl 7k test render. A normal person would have killed one of the processes involved and let failures cascade to the others. But killing the whole group simultaneously strikes me as cleaner.

Process group signaling isn't some exotic operation. You use it all the time. Every time you ^C a command, the tty sends SIGINT to the foreground process group. Interactive shells run all but the simplest commands in a new process group, which among other things makes job control possible.

Process group signaling is in fact an awesome Unix innovation. I love it so much I added it to daemontools , where svc -+h now avoids orphans in a multiprocess service bounce.

At any rate, imagine my surprise when the command didn't just kill those render processes, but killed all processes on the machine save one!

Here's the relevant snippet from procps 4.0.4 , the provider of /bin/kill in Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Can you spot the bug?

opterr = 0 ; /* suppress errors on -123 */

while (( i = getopt_long ( argc , argv , "l::Ls:hVq:" , longopts , & optindex )) != - 1 )

xwarnx ( _ ( "invalid argument %c" ), optopt );

/* Special case for signal digit negative

if ( ! execute_kill (( pid_t ) pid , signo , use_sigqueue , sigval ))

My initial guess was wrong. There's no underflow or overflow bug with -1490947 .

Notice we're in the unrecognized option switch case. Here's what getopt(3) says about unrecognized options:

By default, getopt() prints an error message on standard error, places the erroneous option character in optopt, and returns '?' as the function result.

If pid equals -1, then sig is sent to every process for which the calling process has permission to send signals, except for process 1 (init).

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Linus Torvalds says Linux kernel is out of 'stabilization phase' and using 'much healthier model' for AI contributions
items.content:
Linus Torvalds says Linux kernel is out of 'stabilization phase' and using 'much healthier model' for AI contributions

Yet machine-made patches ‘often get rewritten’

Nvidia is happy to take your money whether you're using open or closed models, says Jensen Huang

British fintech Revolut slashes AI coding costs 10x by cutting out Claude and going self-hosted

AI policy wonks declare 'sovereign agents' a threat to civilization

Pokémon bakeoff reveals best JavaScript frameworks for AI

Forget retraining - AI can now tweak another AI's weights

Linus Torvalds has posted the first release candidate for version 7.4 of the Linux kernel and offered his opinion that the project has found a “much healthier model” for using AI.

“This is a *BIG* merge window,” he wrote in his weekly state of the kernel update , as it contains almost 20,000 commits compared to the usual ~15,000 that developers submit for a new cut of the kernel.

“I think the reason is the by now obvious one, but I'm actually taking it as a good sign: I'm *much* happier with the flood of AI triggered work going into the merge window than it showing up mainly as extra fixes during the -rc period.”

He therefore hopes that the unusually large number of commits “is a sign that the AI fixes are becoming more part of the ‘normal development’ than a flood of fixes that go into the whole stabilization phase."

“I think that's a much healthier model,” he added, before hedging with the observation that “people are expecting 7.4 to be the next LTS [long-term support] release, which is another independent reason why some releases tend larger than others.”

“So it may not *just* be the flood of AI patches.”

Torvalds also seems not to be completely convinced that all AI submissions are entirely helpful, by describing this release as “Large, and full of fixes for issues found by AI (and more and more the patches have been suggested by AI too, although they often get rewritten).”

AMD GPU register offsets and bit masks make up a third of the changes this time around.

“We've been here before, and I'm sure we'll see it many times again in the future,” Torvalds wrote. “Just ignore the noise.”

The kernel-watchers at Phoronix rate the major inclusions in Linux 7.4 as improved support for processors from AMD, Apple, and Google. Other additions include some handy tweaks to improve security for virtual machines, support for the Raspberry Pi 10-inch monitor and more work to get Linux running happily on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 SoC for PCs. ®

items.title: kitty 0.50.0
items.summary: release, unix
items.content:
kitty is a feature-rich, cross-platform, fast , GPU based terminal.

To update kitty , follow the instructions .

Choose an edge when resizing [unreleased] ¶

The resize page now offers two strategies: Window retains the usual

width/height controls, while Edge lets you choose an internal pane edge in

the Splits layout and move its divider in a physical direction.

Press H to select the middle pane’s left edge. Gray edges are outside

After selecting H, Alt+H moves the left divider by one third of the

remaining resize steps. The right divider stays in place. ¶

Switch strategies with 1/2 inside the page. Each strategy remembers its own

Alt/Shift modifier and fraction, configurable with M and F. A sole internal

edge is selected automatically. In Splits, either strategy uses R to restore

the proportions saved when resize mode opened. See Resizing windows for

kitty now has official support for Custom Shaders . These can be used for all

manner of graphical effects, from animated backgrounds to focus highlighting to

animations that change how cursor movements or mouse clicks are visualised.

See the documentation for a video gallery showcasing various custom shaders

This release saw tons of performance work focused on improving throughput

making kitty even faster than it already is. Real world effective throughput

should see a 15-35% improvement depending on workload. Some details:

Improve throughput when processing large amounts of text with a scrollback buffer much larger than the CPU cache by ~35% by prefetching scrollback memory before it is written to

Improve throughput when processing large amounts of text by ~50% for ASCII and ~15% for Unicode by writing runs of plain ASCII chars to the screen in batches and skipping unnecessary bookkeeping in the scrolling and tab handling hot paths

Speed up SIMD UTF-8 decoding: ~20% faster for ASCII and ~50% faster for multi-byte text on both x86 and ARM, by processing pairs of vectors of plain ASCII text at a time and compacting decoded codepoints within 128-bit lanes, avoiding expensive cross-lane operations. Also add an AVX-512 based decoder, another ~75% faster for multi-byte text, used automatically on CPUs that support it (Intel Ice Lake+, AMD Zen 4+).

Improve throughput when processing escape code heavy input by ~30% by taking the input buffer lock once per buffer of input rather than once per escape code and using cheaper arithmetic to parse CSI parameters

Improve throughput when processing large amounts of plain text by another ~10% by finding runs of printable ASCII chars with SIMD , filling cells using wide stores and skipping unnecessary work in the scrolling hot path when there are no images

Speed up pixel compositing with SIMD vectorization: alpha blending of graphics protocol images and animation frames is 2-3.5x faster and glyph alpha masks are composited onto canvases using the same vectorized primitives.

Cache HarfBuzz results for repeated short runs (≤32 cells) so redraws of the same on-screen text are not reshaped

kitty now has support for vertical tabs along the left or right edge of the OS

Window. Useful for people that have wide aspect ratio windows.

Drag and drop for terminal programs [0.47] ¶

kitty now has a new Drag and Drop kitten that allows you to seamlessly

items.title: Sam Altman Crows That AI Is Now Smarter Than the Brightest Human Scientists: Sure, Sam.
items.content:
AI companies sure have a funny marketing strategy.

When they’re not too busy predicting how their own tech will destroy the world , they like to insist that AI is well on its way to — or already has — surpassed the cognitive ability of humans. They’re grabbing customers by the shoulders, looking them dead in the eye, and telling them that they’ve now been rendered inferior beings. They’ll be honored, they seem to believe, to be a stepping stone towards progress (or tortured for eternity by a vindictive superintelligence for trying to stop AI from being brought about, according to certain utterly delusional corners of Silicon Valley.)

And that brings us to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Speaking at a conference in Abu Dhabi this week, Altman, whose company is under fire right now for allegedly disrespecting the entire field of mathematics , stressed that people should remain in control of the future, not AI. That’s when he snuck in a little side claim: that AI has now eclipsed even the brightest scientists — hence why it’s more urgent than ever that we keep a handle on our own destiny.

At the start of this year, “AI was mostly not as smart as our smartest scientists. And now it’s mostly smarter than them,” Altman said at the conference, in conversation with the editor-in-chief of the UAE state-owned paper The National .

Altman and OpenAI have long banged on about the intelligence of its models with respect to human scholars. When it released GPT-5 last year, it touted it as having “PhD-levels” of intelligence, and was routinely mocked for that obviously not being the case. Altman has also frequently predicted that AI will surpass human intelligence by the end of the decade.

This year, the “PhD-level” claim actually appeared to come true, sort of. OpenAI announced that it found a solution to the Navier-Stokes equations as laid out in the famous Millennium Prize Problems, something no human mathematician had ever solved. That caused a blowup ( get it? ) because a mathematician accused OpenAI of unfairly using his research, fueling discussions about how OpenAI was treating the math community.

OpenAI then poured fuel on the tire — or should we say, threw tons of paper on it — by simultaneously releasing hundreds of studies documenting purported solutions to even more math problems. Prominent mathematicians were incensed at how the community was being treated as unpaid proofreaders for OpenAI’s mountain of output, while OpenAI got to glorify their model as already matching their human intellect.

For Altman to come out and say that AI is now smarter than scientists when he has a significant chunk of the scientific community gunning for him is, shall we say, a choice. It’s also a claim that needs proof. The math fiasco is a good example of why it remains dubious. While the solutions appear technically correct, the actual natural language of the AI proofs are borderline incomprehensible , and it will probably take researchers years to unpack them all. As such, their actual utility to the field remains questionable.

items.title: Bupleurum oslaense — critically endangered herb from the Western Himalayas
items.content:
General Botanists discover critically endangered plant species in Uttarakhand

Botanists from the Botanical Survey of India have discovered and described a brand-new plant species, named Bupleurum oslaense, in the temperate forests of the Western Himalayas. Found by researchers ...

Bupleurum oslaense (credits -authors of the study https://doi.org/10.1002/njb.05225) Credit: Authors of the study

Botanists from the Botanical Survey of India have discovered and described a brand-new plant species, named Bupleurum oslaense , in the temperate forests of the Western Himalayas. Found by researchers Jayanta Ghosh, Manas Bhaumik, and Priyanka Bhandari, the new perennial herb was spotted during a field exploration tour in July 2024. The specimens were collected specifically from the streamside rocky walls near Osla village, situated at an elevation of roughly 2,550 meters within the Govind Pashu Vihar National Park and Sanctuary in Uttarakhand, India.

The discovery was brought to light through a combination of field exploration, traditional plant taxonomy, and modern molecular science. During their expedition, the researchers gathered plant samples and preserved fresh leaves in silica gel for DNA extraction. Back in the laboratory, they isolated the genomic DNA and analysed the nuclear ribosomal internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region using phylogenetic tools like maximum likelihood and Bayesian inference analyses. They cross-referenced these genetic data with extensive herbarium records across national and international repositories, including major archives in China and Bhutan, to confirm that the samples genuinely represented a species new to science.

The plant's scientific name pays homage to its geographical origins; the specific epithet oslaense is derived directly from 'Osla', the remote village near where the specimens were collected. While B. oslaense shares genetic and structural similarities with Bupleurum petiolulatum (a relative native to China), it possesses several unique physical characteristics that easily set it apart. Standing up to 80 centimetres tall with a sturdy, stout habit, the new species features narrower lower leaves, broader upper leaves with distinct red-tinged margins, larger bracts numbering between three and five, and flower clusters (umbellules) packing 10 to 20 flowers each. Furthermore, its broadly ovoid fruits with slightly winged ribs distinguish it from the ellipsoid or oblongoid fruits of its Chinese counterpart.

Because the researchers found only a single population consisting of just three mature individuals confined to a restricted 4-square-kilometre area, the species faces an extremely high risk of local extinction. Consequently, following strict International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) guidelines, Bupleurum oslaense has been formally assessed and categorised as "Critically Endangered." This discovery once again underscores the vast biodiversity residing within Himalayan ecosystems and highlights an urgent need for targeted, long-term conservation monitoring to protect fragile habitats from vanishing forever.

items.content_ko: Apache ActiveMQ 및 ActiveMQ Broker에서 OOM(메모리 부족)으로 인한 서비스 거부(DoS) 취약점이 확인되었습니다. 인증된 OpenWire 클라이언트가 다른 연결이 소유한 임시 큐/토픽에 대해 ConsumerInfo를 보내면 InvalidDestinationException으로 거부되지만, 거부된 Subscription이 브로커 영역(region)의 subscriptions 맵에 남습니다. 같은 요청을 반복하면 브로커가 거부된 subscription을 정리하지 않아 힙 메모리가 계속 누수되고 결국 OOM이 발생합니다. 영향 버전은 Apache ActiveMQ 6.0.0 이상 6.3.3 미만, 5.19.12 미만이며, ActiveMQ Broker도 같은 범위입니다. 수정 버전은 6.4.0, 6.3.3, 5.19.12이며 해당 버전으로 업그레이드할 것이 권장됩니다. 입력 정보 기준 CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False로 표시되어 있습니다. 공개일은 2026-11-04입니다.

items.content:
Dear Lobste.rs, over a year after my previous post on mouse free setups , your advice was instrumental to building the tech stack I use today as a disabled person, composed of the Svalboard, Talon Voice, and a fair few extensions for Talon (including ones I've written myself.)

One aspect of my work and personal life that has remained stubbornly able-bodied has been, surprisingly, my terminal use. Reading, manipulating, and editing the terminal has required keyboard and mouse use at every step:

I am fairly convinced there is no true voice first terminal experience-- this is something I am hoping to change. In order to accomplish this and maybe make my life easier, I want to know the landscape of how various people interact with their terminals in 2026. I feel like my approach is deeply inefficient and must be missing something obvious...? We've had terminals since before mice existed, surely there are better ways.

When writing a terminal command, things can range from easy to brutal. Talon has a lot of built in terminal commands available, but composing complex commands still requires a great deal of typing. The most irritating aspect to me is editing a previous command, which consists of either holding (Ctrl+) an arrow key and waiting until I hit the right character, often overshooting, and then having to go back the opposite direction with the arrow keys again, OR moving with my mouse and clicking on the correct position.

is the problem the shell/terminal itself lacking editor a11y features? or the syntax/structure of the shell commands? if it is an editor problem, does your shell support "open command in editor"? i know fish and bash (via C-x C-e by default) do, which might let you take greater advantage of your other tools.

I scroll the view using keybinds that are default in many terminal emulators, namely ctrl+shift+up, ctrl+shift+down, shift+pgup, and shift+pgdown. It seems also that ghostty has the ability to configure keybinds to adjust the selection , which may be of interest to you

I am fairly convinced there is no true voice first terminal experience-- this is something I am hoping to change

I've written a terminal e-mail client. If I want to make my terminal app usable by voice, what assistive software stack should I use for development? I am aware of things like AccessKit but that's geared to graphical user interfaces.

Since my client is a library with a terminal front end, I do not even need to retrofit this kind of accessibility, I can just write a new front end.

The most irritating aspect to me is editing a previous command,

Friend, let me tell you about the fc command. fc -l lists the last few commands. fc and a number edits that command in your favorite $EDITOR and then when you save/exit it runs it!

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title_ko: 제로데이 취약점, Windows 11 BitLocker 기본 보호 완전히 우회
items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Anthropic Debuts Tool for Your Boss to Spy on Your Claude Chats: The tool will tell bosses "how a team uses Claude" and "report on the work getting done."
items.content:
Anthropic seems hellbent on making itself one of the most hated companies among white collar workers.

The AI lab behind the chatbot Claude has announced a new feature, “Smart Reports,” which is meant to allow managers to scrape and analyze their employee’s workaday interactions with Anthropic ‘s various AI products.

According to Anthropic’s Smart Reports support page , the tool will let bosses generate summaries based on “how a team uses Claude” in order to “report on the work getting done” throughout the day. Anthropic claims that its system will anonymize sessions, though it remains to be seen how secure this system is in practice. (Anthropic’s previous foray into “anonymized” data was a privacy disaster, as the information was easily de-anonymized using common large language models.)

Smart Reports isn’t just about monitoring individual chat sessions. As Anthropic’s support page makes clear, management can use Smart Reports to sort their workers’ AI output by overall cost as well as the chatbot’s output, allowing direct oversight over employee’s perceived efficiency when using AI tools.

The new feature seems to be part of Anthropic’s drive to scoop up enterprise-level contracts as it looks ahead to its IPO . Corporate customers account for a reported 80 percent of Anthropic’s total business, while individual consumer subscriptions make up the rest.

That being the case, Anthropic’s performance on the stock market depends almost entirely on how successfully it can court enterprise customers with products like Smart Reports — the ultimate utility of which remains to be determined.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-111038 📢 Source: INCIBE 💣 CVSS Score: 7.3 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True CSV formula injection vulnerability in the export functionality of the Coupa Supplier Portal SaaS platform. The vulnerability arises because certain user-controlled data, such as event names or templates within the Tenders module, are not properly validated or sanitised before being included in CSV files generated by the application. An attacker with low privileges can input specially crafted values that begin with characters interpreted as formulas by spreadsheet applications. items.summary_ko: Coupa Supplier Portal의 내보내기 기능에서 CSV 수식 주입(CSV formula injection) 취약점 CVE-2026-111038이 확인되었습니다. 권한이 낮은 공격자가 입력한 값이 CSV 파일에 수식으로 포함될 수 있으며, 피해자가 해당 파일을 스프레드시트에서 열면 DDE 등을 통한 명령 실행이나 정보 접근 등이 발생할 수 있습니다. 입력 정보 기준 CVSS 점수는 7.3(HIGH)이며 원격 악용 가능으로 표시되어 있습니다.
items.content_ko: Coupa Supplier Portal SaaS 플랫폼의 내보내기(export) 기능에서 CSV 수식 주입(CSV formula injection) 취약점이 확인되었습니다. Tenders 모듈의 이벤트 이름이나 템플릿 등 사용자가 입력하는 데이터가 CSV 파일 생성 전에 적절히 검증되거나 무해화(sanitize)되지 않습니다. 권한이 낮은 공격자가 스프레드시트 프로그램에서 수식으로 해석되는 문자로 시작하는 값을 입력할 수 있습니다. 피해자가 생성된 파일을 내려받아 호환 프로그램에서 열면 내용이 수식으로 해석될 수 있으며, 이로 인해 DDE 등을 통한 명령 실행, 정보 접근, 피해자 권한으로의 시스템 자원 상호작용 등 승인되지 않은 동작이 발생할 수 있습니다. 입력 정보 기준 CVSS 점수는 7.3(HIGH), 원격 악용 가능 여부는 True이며, 출처는 INCIBE입니다. 공개일은 2026-11-04입니다.
